subject: Hosted API latency spike — action plan and customer communication
body:
From: Robert Cheng <robert.cheng@apexhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: apex-support@apexhealth.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in Hosted API latency — production impacts

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a sharp regression in p95/p99 latency and an uptick in 5xx rate around 08:45 PDT this morning across our production traffic. Impacts:
- p95 increased from ~220ms to ~1.2s, p99 hitting ~2.8s
- 5xxs rose from 0.03% to ~1.1% (primarily 429s and some 500s)
- Request backlog on the /v1/generate endpoint — retries from our side are compounding the load

This is hitting user-facing functionality and our SLOs. We have some customers seeing timeouts. Attached is a compressed dump of our client-side traces (p95-dumps-0809.json) and a Grafana snapshot. Can you escalate to platform ops and leadership? We need an ETA for stabilization and a suggested mitigation we can communicate to internal stakeholders.

Thanks,
Robert
Principal Engineering Manager
ApexHealth

-----------------------------

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Robert Cheng <robert.cheng@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in Hosted API latency — production impacts

Robert — thank you for the quick heads up and for the traces. I am escalating immediately and copying platform and CS. Initial plan:
1) Triage (now): ops to confirm root cause and isolate affected backend pools.
2) Immediate mitigations (next 30–60 min): divert new requests from the affected pool, enable temporary rate limit for large-sequence jobs, and enable fallback routing to an alternate model variant with lower mem/latency.
3) Short term (1–3 hrs): scale dedicated nodes and drain backlog.
4) Customer comms: Marissa to publish a short status update once we have confirmed mitigations.

Can platform folks confirm whether queuing/batching backlog is the source? If so, quick wins include reducing max_batch_size, lowering max_queue_latency, and temporarily disabling very-large-seq batching.

I will update leadership in 60 minutes unless we resolve sooner.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

-----------------------------

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in Hosted API latency — production impacts

Vanessa, team — quick triage notes from ops on-call:
- Observed a rapid increase in queue depth on the primary hosted pool servicing ApexHealth at ~08:42 PDT. Backlog grew when a handful of long-sequence customer jobs entered simultaneously and hit continuous-batching windows.
- Autoscaler did not react quickly enough because the surge was short and the policy requires 4x sustained CPU/GPU utilization for 3m before scale-out.
- Large-sequence requests held KV caches longer, delaying tail processing and contributing to p95/p99 regressions.

Immediate actions taken (done):
- Pulled traffic off pool-3 (affected) and routed to pool-7 (warm spare).
- Reduced max_batch_size from 128 -> 48 for the model family serving these requests.
- Lowered max_queue_latency threshold from 200ms -> 80ms to avoid long dwell time in batch queues.
- Enabled fallback to a 4-bit quantized variant for sequences > 1024 tokens for 30 minutes.

Suggested next steps (recommended by ops):
- Create a short-lived surge autoscale policy (override) for the next 2 hours to more aggressively scale on queue_depth metrics. Command to apply (ops runbook):
  rctl scale-policy set --pool pool-3 --override "queue_depth:threshold=15,duration=30s,scale_mult=2"
- Drain existing backlog by increasing worker concurrency on pool-7 while we warm dedicated capacity.
- Post-mortem to examine batching window heuristics; consider dynamic batch sizing by sequence-length distribution.

Attachment: ops-runbook-ref.txt (contains one-liners and dashboards).

— Sean Gallagher
Sr. Platform Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----------------------------

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Robert Cheng <robert.cheng@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Customer update: brief summary and next steps (draft)

Hi Robert — draft status update we plan to send to your internal teams; please let me know if you want changes before I post to your channel:

Subject: Status update — Redwood Hosted API latency spike (Aug 9)

Hi team,

Short update: We observed an elevated p95/p99 and increased 5xx rate affecting the /v1/generate endpoint starting ~08:45 PDT. Redwood has:
- Identified a batching/queueing backlog triggered by concurrent long-sequence requests.
- Rerouted traffic to a warm spare pool and reduced batch sizes to reduce dwell time.
- Enabled temporary fallback to a faster quantized model for the heaviest requests.

What we’re doing now:
- Draining remaining backlog; applying an aggressive, temporary autoscale override to reduce queue depth.
- Monitoring latency and error-rate; we will not change your model config without approval.
- ETA for visible stabilization: 1–2 hours; more detailed post-mortem within 48 hours.

We know this is disruptive — we will follow up with a post-mortem and propose credits if your SLO was materially impacted.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: customer_update_draft-0809.txt

-----------------------------

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in Hosted API latency — action plan and exec escalation

Thanks all for the rapid triage. Current status:
- Latency and 5xx rate have reduced but p99 tails are still slightly elevated relative to baseline.
- Backlog has mostly drained; pool-7 handling residual traffic.
- Ops applied the temporary scale override and we will maintain the reduced batch config for 2 hours.

I am escalating to leadership with the timeline and the mitigation steps we implemented. Laura — please include finance and legal on any customer credit discussion; Marissa, please send the customer-facing update and offer a short credit (we can finalize amount after post-mortem).

Action items assigned:
- Sean: capture metrics and create a short-runbook entry for this class of spike (queue-depth + long-seq).
- Karthik: open a Jira for the batching heuristic post-mortem and assigned owner for follow-up work.
- Marissa: post the customer update and coordinate credit.
- Hannah: schedule a leadership sync for 16:30 PDT to review the incident/state.

I will follow up after the leadership touchpoint. Thanks again for the quick response.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
